value.body: The highest academic degree: several years of original research under a supervisor, ending in a thesis and a viva. It starts with coursework, then moves to your own research and publications. It leads mainly to university teaching, research labs, and research-focused roles in industry and government.

items.label: Duration in India
items.note: Minimum 3 and maximum 6 years under UGC's 2022 PhD regulations, with some extensions allowed

items.label: PhD scholars in India
items.note: Up from ~1.2 lakh in 2014-15; Science (23%) and Engineering (21%) are the largest areas

items.label: JRF / SRF fellowship
items.note: UGC, CSIR and DST rates; many institutes pay their own fellowships to admitted scholars
items.source: UGC and DST fellowship revisions (effective Jan 2023)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: In India: a master's degree with 55% (50% for reserved categories), or a four-year bachelor's degree with 75%. Admission is through UGC-NET / CSIR-NET (JRF or PhD-eligible score), GATE (common at IITs, NITs and IISc for engineering and science), or the university's own entrance test, followed by an interview. Abroad: you apply directly to universities; in the US many PhDs admit after a bachelor's degree and are funded through teaching or research assistantships.

value.title: At a glance
items: The supervisor and lab shape day-to-day work and outcomes as much as the institution does.
Not every PhD seat comes with a fellowship; unfunded scholars cover their own costs for several years.
Holding a JRF lets you join a PhD with a funded fellowship at most universities.
University teaching posts typically require a PhD or NET, and recruitment is separate from the degree.
